statement: For every finite Fano problem except lines on a cubic surface and linear spaces on intersections of two quadrics, the geometric monodromy contains the alternating group on its N solutions, hence is A_N or S_N. For k-planes on two quadrics in P^(2k+2), the monodromy is W(D_(2k+3)) in characteristic different from two.

answer.text: For every finite Fano problem except lines on a cubic surface and linear spaces on intersections of two quadrics, the geometric monodromy contains the alternating group on its N solutions, hence is A_N or S_N. For k-planes on two quadrics in P^(2k+2), the monodromy is W(D_(2k+3)) in characteristic different from two.

notes:
The alternating-versus-symmetric alternative is not resolved in general in this paper; Yahl settles all nonexceptional types of degree <75,000. The two-quadric equality uses char K≠2; complex geometry satisfies this.
